title: EU AML Regulation (AMLR) for investment firms and brokers | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: Investment firms and brokers are obliged entities under the EU AMLR from 10 July 2027: when CDD applies, what AMLA's drafts change and how to prepare.
body_markdown:
*What the EU AMLR and AMLA's final draft standards mean for opening investment accounts, cross-border onboarding and remote identification.*


Investment firms authorised under MiFID II, including online brokers with such an authorisation, are financial institutions and therefore obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies directly from 10 July 2027. An investment firm must apply customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship, such as opening an investment account, and when it carries out an occasional transaction of EUR 10,000 or more, in a single operation or through linked transactions. Under AMLA's final draft standards, remote verification is expected to use suitable eIDs, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet), or relevant qualified trust services wherever possible.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Patryk Pietrzak (Head of Growth), Authologic.*
